To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
M. tuberculosis infection induces a significant up-regulation of DCs in the lung and mediastinal lymph nodes, which are characterized by the expression of maturation and activation markers.
M. tuberculosis infection induces DCs to produce pro-inflammatory cytokines, which in turn stimulate the proliferation of T cells and enhance the production of proinflammatory cytokines.
M. tuberculosis imparts DCs with an ability to stimulate CD4 T cells to produce IFN-Î³ and IL-2, and to induce Th1 and Th17 responses.

the role of DCs in M. tuberculosis infection and the outcome of interaction between these two cells.
